summary: the cases of the selfbuild and selfbuild-ext2 suites on i686, against a kernel whose bytes depend on the time it was compiled, a kernel that reports a processor past the set's limit only when TinyCC compiled it, and an echo that prints a stray byte only when TinyCC compiled it; the guest compiles the sources the faults change, so copies of them are artifacts beside the host's kernel

argv: ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel && cp rach2/kernel.c rach2/sys/syscall_proc.c utils/echo.c ${WORK}/
ARCH=i686 RACH2_WORKERS=4 exec tests/run selfbuild selfbuild-ext2 </dev/null

faults.name: build-time
faults.summary: an unreproducible build: the debug shell's greeting has the time of the compile, so two builds of one tree minutes apart make two kernels

edits.find:
kernel_shell_active = true;
    console_puts("Type 'help' for available commands.");
edits.replace:
kernel_shell_active = true;
    console_puts("Type 'help' for available commands. " __TIME__);

faults.name: tcc-getcpu
faults.summary: a fault of the guest's build alone: getcpu reports processor 4096 when TinyCC compiled the kernel, so callsmusl fails on the kernel the machine built and on no other

faults.name: tcc-echo
faults.summary: a fault of the guest's build alone: echo ends its line with a stray byte when TinyCC compiled it, so the echo the machine built prints the wrong text
